title: Tester: newcomer on a laptop
brief:
Read and follow <scratch> first. You are "nina" (report: nina.md).

Persona: Nina, a first-time visitor on a laptop (1280x900). She has no AI agent of her own and has never heard of Join. A friend sent her the link. She wants karaoke with three friends this weekend for about $15 each.

Do: open the address, understand what it is, make a demo account, and use Join's own agent (the website drawer) to plan the karaoke and get it booked (the PayPal sandbox test card may authorize automatically). Then click through EVERY page in the menu (Activity, Plans, Map, Limits, Connect, Venue view) and try every button, link, card, pin, bar and chip that looks like it does something, including the map's pins and popups and "Show around me". Note each thing that looks clickable but does nothing, each dead end, and each word or screen a first-time person wouldn't understand. Check the receipt of your booking if you get one.

Badminton, karaoke, an escape room, board games, a barbecue, hot pot: Join is the marketplace AI agents come to. They find who is free, negotiate the price with the venue, split the cost and settle it with PayPal, inside the limits you set. No agent? Join's website agent asks what you want and does it for you. Join keeps the rules and shows you everything an agent did.

Why not just split it on Venmo afterwards? Because someone has to book and pay first. Here the venue is paid only when the money is real: the organizer guarantees it in PayPal, each friend pays their own share, and anyone who said yes and didn't pay gets a PayPal invoice. Nobody chases anyone.

Set your limits

VERDICT: 0 BLOCKER, 7 BUG, 11 CONFUSING

I made a demo account and got the karaoke booked through the drawer agent. It ended "Paid and locked" at Echo Karaoke, $23.40 total and $5.85 each. The full report is in `<scratch>`.

Most important findings:
1. **Other testers' data shows up in Nina's account.**
   - **Plans/Activity:** Nina has a badminton booking she never asked for (organizer "Weiting"), already marked "You $7.65 paid", plus a "Join and pay" card.
   - **Map:** the side panel shows that booking instead of Nina's karaoke.
   - **Drawer:** the first search offered a group "Nina, Ines, Mei, Weiting".
2. **The receipt and venue pages are written for engineers.**
   - **Receipt:** it shows hashed player ids, no venue name or friend names, "Waiting for the next batch", and a `node examples/verify-receipt.mjs` command. It is not a booking confirmation a person can show.
   - **Plans:** "Signed authorizations (AP2)" opens raw JSON with cents and dollars mixed.
   - **Drawer header and Show around me:** both show developer text ("Qwen qwen2.5:0.5b", "https or localhost").
   - **Venue view:** "Reconciliation" never finished loading. "Bill extras" says "billed $12.00 (sent)" for Nina's booking, and she never saw an invoice or notice.
3. **Several controls are dead ends or inconsistent.**
   - **Vault:** "Save PayPal for my agent" goes to the real sandbox.paypal.com login page, which a demo user can't use.
   - **Map:** the blue circles and dashed line do nothing when clicked, and "Show around me" visibly does nothing.
   - **Drawer:** a vague message like "hello" gets the same canned reply. The "Go ahead" confirmation appeared in one run and was skipped in another.
   - **Connect:** the Copy button says "Copied", but I couldn't confirm the text reached the clipboard.
